findings.summary: Two shipped hook scripts matched pytest's default discovery pattern while being guards, not tests, and the same basename was vendored into up to three trees of one repo. A downstream repo whose CI hands changed files to pytest aborted collection with 'import file mismatch', failing its gate and blocking its push. Latent since Codex vendoring; detonated by a routine refresh.
findings.disposition: Renamed to lock_guard.py / weakening_guard.py. Two alternative remedies were empirically TESTED and rejected first: conftest collect_ignore_glob does not apply to explicitly-passed paths, and __init__.py does not resolve the basename clash. The standing check asserts the INVARIANT (no vendored file matches pytest discovery) rather than the two names, so a future collectible guard fails on the day it is added.

findings.summary: The rename alone fixes only NEW installs. The installer never deleted anything, so every repo that already vendored the old guards would keep the stale copy beside the new one — still collectible, still colliding, still breaking that repo's gate. A fix that reaches nobody who already has us is the same shape as the bug it fixes.
findings.disposition: Two mechanisms. GENERAL and derived: files the previous manifest claims we wrote that are absent from the current roster are removed, so the next rename needs no migration code. BOUNDED and dated: a frozen LEGACY_COLLECTIBLE list, because the trees carrying the broken names predate manifests and the derived prune has no input there. Both narrow to paths we claimed; a user's own file in a vendored directory is never touched.

findings.summary: Every test in this repo passed for the entire lifetime of the defect. The failure exists only inside a CONSUMER's test runner, so no amount of coverage here could have seen it — the Playbook failed its own seam-you-don't-own rule against itself, and its own §5b doctrine names exactly this shape.
findings.disposition: Closed by PROVING the fix at the seam rather than in unit tests alone: the consumer's tree was reproduced (3 collection errors observed), the fixed installer run against it, and collection verified clean. The unit tests are the regression net; the reproduction is the evidence the net is pointed at the real failure.
